questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Which of the following insects can live for weeks without its head?
A. Grasshopper
B. Butterfly
C. Cockroach
Answer: C. A cockroach can survive without its head for several weeks, eventually dying from starvation or thirst.
questions.en: Which insect, a byword for toughness, can survive for weeks without its head, eventually dying of thirst or starvation?
questions.de: Welches für seine Zähigkeit berüchtigte Insekt kann wochenlang ohne Kopf überleben und stirbt schließlich an Durst oder Hunger?

timeline.labelDe: Früheste schabenartige Fossilien (Roachoiden) aus dem Karbon

source.title: Fact or Fiction?: A Cockroach Can Live without Its Head

questions.notes: Scientific American (2007, Joseph Kunkel): decapitated American cockroaches lasted several weeks. Wikipedia notes popular longevity claims lack published research, and other insects also survive decapitation. German also 'Kakerlake'.

questions.cardText:
[Astronomy] What are pulsars known for?
A. Moving faster through space than any other celestial object
B. Being the remnants of black holes
C. Emitting beams of radiation
Answer: C. Pulsars are incredibly dense, with masses greater than that of the sun but only the size of a small city. A teaspoon of a pulsar would be heavier than hundreds of the Great Pyramid of Giza combined.
questions.en: What do pulsars, rapidly rotating neutron stars, emit from their magnetic poles?
questions.de: Was senden Pulsare, schnell rotierende Neutronensterne, von ihren Magnetpolen aus?

timeline.labelEn: Jocelyn Bell discovers the first pulsar
timeline.labelDe: Jocelyn Bell entdeckt den ersten Pulsar

questions.notes: Pulsars are neutron stars, not remnants of black holes (option B is wrong on both counts).
